rows.comment: Short source label; states the fact.
Screen title; informal but short and clear.
States where data comes from and where it is derived.
Terse status label on a developer-facing screen. 'Gated' is jargon but the row is a nerd-stats flag.
Gives the reason for the empty state.
Defines the metric with its 70 ms threshold; do not alter the number.
Abbreviated label for a developer-facing row; no better wording is known without the surrounding code.
'Carried' is figurative and 'bin' is used as a verb without being defined.
lineComments: Say what happened to the night.
rows.replacement: 'Too few clean beats to split this night into bins.'

rows.comment: Em dash, 'carried enough beats' and a long listing of causes in one sentence. The point that the chart cannot explain the night is worth keeping.
lineComments: Interpolations kept; 'carried enough beats to' becomes 'had enough beats to'.
Em dash removed; the causes list stays.
rows.replacement:
'$drawn of ${bins.length} bins had enough beats to read. '
'The rest are gaps, not zeroes. '
"The outer pair is the estimator's own sampling spread, not a range you were in. "
'This describes the night and cannot explain it. '
'A low first third fits alcohol, a late meal, late training, '
'a warm room, an illness starting, or nothing at all.'

rows.comment: Em dash and a stacked 'no X, and none exists' claim. Keeps the fact that no reference range exists.
lineComments: Reframes as what the line compares against.
States the missing reference range once.
rows.replacement:
'This line compares only your own nights. No reference range exists '
'for pulse arrivals. Signal quality varies by night and moves '
'this line on its own; last night counted '
'${thousands(beats)} beats.'

rows.comment: Em dash and stacked claim; same fix as the sibling string.
lineComments: Reframes as what the line compares against.

rows.replacement:
'This line compares only your own nights. No reference range exists '
'for pulse arrivals. Signal quality varies by night and moves '
'this line on its own.'

rows.comment: Fragment of a pluralisation expression split by the extractor; the prose continues in the next row.

Stacked 'not a negative result; this is a screen' antithesis. Keeps the warning that a clear strip rules nothing out, since this is a health-screen safety statement. This is the tail of the pluralised sentence, so the fragment form is kept.
lineComments: Lists what it cannot tell apart.
rows.replacement:
'}, raised its flag on '
'$raised. An outlined square is a day it did not run. A clear '
'strip does not rule anything out. The screen reads pulse '
'timing and cannot tell an ectopic beat from a dropped beat '
'or from the band moving on your wrist.'

rows.comment: Em dash and an unrequested reassurance ('not a day anything went wrong'). Keeps the three-minute window and still-stretch condition.
lineComments: Keeps the three-minute stretch and still condition.
Gives the cause of the empty state.
rows.replacement:
'This reads breathing only from three-minute stretches where the '
'band saw you almost completely still, outside the sleep '
'window. Most days have none because you were moving '
'throughout.'

rows.comment: Opens with an 'A floor, not X' antithesis and has an em dash. The limit it describes (only still stretches can be read) is useful and kept.
lineComments: Says what the numbers are instead of the 'floor' metaphor.
Describes the stillest minutes outside sleep.
Drops the em dash and the 'nothing here' phrasing.
rows.replacement:
'These are the lowest readings of the day, not a daily rate. Only stretches where you were '
'almost completely still can be read, so they come from the '
'stillest few minutes the band saw outside your sleep and say '
'nothing about the rest of your day. Breathing while you '
'move cannot be recovered from beat timing.'

rows.comment: 'Several' and 'a few' are vague. The minimum night and hour counts live in the analytics sibling package, not this repo, so no number can be cited here. Replacement says only what the screen needs.
rows.replacement: 'This view needs more nights, each with enough observed hours to count cycles.'

rows.comment: States a count and the reason for exclusion.
States a count and the reason.
Section header with the night count.
'Running higher than across' is clumsy; 'behind it' is vague.
rows.replacement:
'Over your most recent nights, the heart-rate cycling '
'this screen counts has run higher than over '
'the $n nights before them.'

rows.comment: Same clumsy phrasing as the sibling string.
rows.replacement:
'Over your most recent nights, the heart-rate cycling '
'this screen counts has stayed within the range of '
'the $n nights before them.'

rows.comment: Stacked 'not X, not Y' negations and an em dash. The medical caveats are kept because they are safety statements; the repo holds no citation for them, so none is added.
lineComments: States plainly it does not measure breathing or test anything.
Lists the other causes of the same cycling.
Keeps the drugs and conditions that flatten the signal.
Keeps the consequence for disturbed breathing.
rows.replacement:
'This is a pattern in your pulse. It does not measure your '
'breathing and is not a test for anything. An irregular rhythm, '
'altitude and any broken-up night produce the same '
'cycling. Beta-blockers, '
'diabetes and nerve conditions flatten it, so disturbed '
'breathing can leave nothing here at all.'

rows.comment: Triple 'nothing here' phrasing and an em dash. The caveat that no result clears the user is kept.
lineComments: Moves the em-dash clause into its own sentence.
Ends with the reason single-night counts vary.
rows.replacement:
"No result here rules anything out. "
"A single night's count says little on its own "
"because it moves for many reasons."

rows.comment: Safety advice kept; 'test that properly' is vague about what to ask for.
rows.replacement:
'If you snore, wake unrefreshed, or someone has seen you '
'stop breathing in your sleep, ask a clinician '
'about a sleep test.'
